clue.text: Extremes of terror in air — with weapons, treats violently

indicators.note: the extreme letters of terror are placed inside the word for air

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from terror

parts.note: arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Someone in a frightening aerial situation, armed, is roughing people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To strong-arm someone is to use force or bullying against them, treating them violently.

clue.text: Doctor carrying one walked across a rough track

indicators.note: the abbreviation for doctor carries, or holds, the numeral inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for walked lies across, straddling, the letter A

parts.note: trod is a past tense of tread, to walk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying a patient trudges over a bumpy path.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt road is an unpaved road, which is a rough track for vehicles.

clue.text: State of 16 22 down, emphatically not without monarch

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the phrase surrounds the letter for monarch

parts.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Someone firmly refuses that a country with a red, white and blue flag has no king.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is RED WHITE AND BLUE and 22 down is FLAG, so the definition is a state whose flag has those colours. 'Without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a sovereign nation, and its flag is red with a white-bordered blue cross.

clue.text: Literary work in English penned by Englishman

indicators.note: penned means shut in like an animal in a pen, so the letter sits inside the word for Englishman

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person

explanation.surface: A piece of writing in English was written by an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned by' suggests authorship, but it means enclosed: E goes inside POM, Australian slang for an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem is a piece of literature in verse, so a literary work.

clue.text: Informant and sneak, possibly, but a harmless crawler

parts.note: a grass is British slang for a police informer

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of sneak may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone who informs and sneaks around turns out to be fairly harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASS is British slang for one who informs to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass snake is a non-venomous European snake, so a harmless creature that crawls.

clue.text: Credited as copied, using only one book

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cribbed has a double B, and only one of them is kept, so one is removed

parts.note: to crib is to copy someone else's work

explanation.surface: A student is given credit for copied work drawn from a single textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something to someone is to credit or attribute it to them.

clue.text: Greek woman love has uplifted, covering pages

indicators.note: the turned letters cover, or enclose, the abbreviation for pages
in a down clue, uplifted means the words for love and has are read from bottom to top

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek woman in love has been raised up, protecting some pages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifted' means read upwards, turning O and the word has round; 'covering' then wraps them round the pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was an ancient Greek lyric poet from Lesbos, a celebrated woman of Greece.

clue.text: Divine female leads a double life

indicators.note: a double life is one lived twice over, so the word for being alive is written twice

parts.note: to have life is to exist, and a thing that exists is, in the plain sense of to be

explanation.surface: A goddess is secretly living two separate lives.
explanation.walkthrough: To lead a life is to be, so IS; a double life is IS IS. 'Leads a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a goddess of ancient Egypt, a female deity.

clue.text: Right places passed over in trip — one flies over Paris, for example

definitions.text: one flies over Paris, for example

indicators.note: the right letter and turned places are put in the word for trip

parts.note: a tour is a trip

indicators.note: passed over is read as turned over, so the word for places is reversed

parts.note: loci is the plural of locus, a place

explanation.surface: Someone on a journey skipped some places, and a plane flies over Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' looks like skipped, but it means flipped over, so the word for places is read backwards before going into the trip with R.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national flag, the tricolour, flies over Paris, the capital being one example of where it flies.

clue.text: Has important role as crewman in vessel

indicators.note: the sailor sits in the abbreviation for a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
a tar is a sailor, a crewman on a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor plays a key part on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who stars takes the leading part, so has an important role.

clue.text: Old-fashioned religious teacher mainly excelled in crawling

parts.note: something out of fashion is said to be out

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a swami is a Hindu religious teacher

explanation.surface: A dated guru was good at swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawling' is the swimming stroke, the front crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To outswim someone is to beat them at swimming, so excelled at the front crawl stroke.

clue.text: Bunk in ship as indication of rank

indicators.note: the nonsense word is placed in the abbreviation for a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
bunk is nonsense, as is tripe

explanation.surface: A sailor's bunk on a ship shows his position in the hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed on board, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes worn on a sleeve are chevrons showing a soldier's or officer's grade, so they indicate rank.

clue.text: Celebrity, when old, 10 and 12

definitions.meaning: fame or renown, the state of being celebrated
with old in front, it is the nickname of the US flag, the stars and stripes

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is STARS and 12 is STRIPES; Old Glory is a nickname for the Stars and Stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory is great fame and honour, synonymous with celebrity in the sense of renown.

clue.text: Medical records, one of which describes work of consultant assisted by doctor

definitions.meaning: books in which a doctor keeps notes of patients' cases

definitions.text: one of which describes work of consultant assisted by doctor
definitions.meaning: The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes tells of the consulting detective, helped by Dr Watson

explanation.walkthrough: The consultant is Sherlock Holmes, a consulting detective, and the doctor is Watson.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's records of cases are kept in volumes, and one Holmes collection carries the same title.

clue.text: Bitter and striking, ie ceasing to work

parts.note: a bitter remark is a cutting one
workers on strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: A biting, hard-hitting comment, namely that something has stopped running.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that is cutting out is stalling, stopping working.

clue.text: Son laments money made in form of gambling

parts.note: to weep is to lament
the take is the money taken in, the takings

explanation.surface: A son mourns the cash he made through betting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery-style bet where all stakes go to the winners, a kind of gambling.

clue.text: Standard description for 9, 25, 10 and 12

parts.note: a standard is a flag, and the French tricolour, Union Jack and Stars and Stripes all share the same three colours

explanation.surface: A conventional account of several other answers in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is TRICOLOUR, 25 UNION JACK, 10 and 12 STARS and STRIPES; 'Standard' means flag, not normal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French, British and American flags all use the colours red, white and blue.

clue.text: See 20
Miss a moment of glory, hence expression of regret

parts.note: to miss something is to lack it
someone who has had their day has enjoyed their time of success

explanation.surface: Missing out on a moment of triumph prompts a sigh of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackaday is an archaic interjection of sorrow, like alas, voicing regret.

clue.text: At sea as number one in warship

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, as the leading vessel among the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like part of the definition, but it signals an anagram of AS, NUMBER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a naval vessel, a warship that operates underwater.

clue.text: Prohibitionist's main policy that's prominently printed in paper

parts.note: one who bans things is a banner
head as an adjective means chief or main
a party line is a policy

explanation.surface: A temperance campaigner's chief aim appears in bold type in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner headline runs across the full width of a newspaper's front page in large type.

clue.text: King leaves reinforcements in Lancashire town

indicators.note: the letter for king leaves, or departs from, the word for reinforcements

parts.note: backup is support or reinforcements
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch abandons his support troops in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: BACUP is a small town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a market town in the Rossendale valley in Lancashire, England.

clue.text: Part of hand with slippery skin

definitions.text: Part of hand with slippery skin

parts.words: Part of hand with slippery skin
parts.note: a hand is also a bunch of a certain yellow fruit whose peel is famously slippery

explanation.walkthrough: The hand is a cluster of fruit, not the body part; one item of the bunch has a skin people slip on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of this fruit is called a hand, and its skin is the classic slapstick slip hazard.

clue.text: Strange feeling for cricketer

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of feeling are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: An odd sensation for a cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG is a cricket fielding position behind the batter on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder stationed at that position is himself called fine leg, a cricketer.

clue.text: Stone sink

definitions.meaning: a flat paving slab, a flagstone
to tire or droop, to lose energy

explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is a paving stone, and to flag is to weaken or decline.

clue.text: Friend and worker following a method of signalling

parts.note: William Penn was a Quaker, a member of the Society of Friends
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A friend and a colleague are using signals to communicate.
explanation.walkthrough: A Friend with a capital F is a Quaker; William Penn, founder of Pennsylvania, was one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennant is a long tapering flag, which ships fly to send signals.

clue.text: Piano tune as duet

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A piano melody played as a piece for two.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a performance by two, and a pair is a set of two.

clue.text: Didn't go to restaurant or pub after eight, say

indicators.note: say signals the words are spoken, the sound being what counts

parts.note: an inn is a pub, so the phrase gives the number eight followed by inn

explanation.surface: Someone stayed home for dinner rather than going out to eat or drinking late.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home rather than dining out at a restaurant.

clue.text: Organised workers given raise that symbolises national merger

parts.note: a trade union is an organisation of workers
to jack something up is to raise it

explanation.surface: Unionised staff get a pay rise, a sign of a coming merger.
explanation.walkthrough: The UNION JACK is the UK flag, combining the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The British flag combines national crosses, a symbol of the union of the kingdoms.
